chapter: Louis Armstrong, King Oliver and St. Louis memories
title: Louis Armstrong's private cab driver Red
summary: Dance asks about Louis. Thomas recounts a St. Louis cab driver, Red, who refused to drive him because Armstrong was in town and had hired him.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, we haven't said much about Louis, you know. You haven't said much about him at all.

He was the greatest cat that ever lived. I called him Pops and we had a thing happen, it was back in St. Louis now. Well, during that time, we'd been to Grossingers, I'd taken my band up to Grossingers, the Vanguard
How big a band did you have up there? At Grossingers?
Five. I have some pictures for you, too.

Oh, I'd say around '46 or '47. But, we're talking about, jumping back to '28 now. This day I'd bought myself a new suit, Stan, and I'd got this new suit. I had a cat over there that plays ... so he says, You want another suit, huh? I said, Yeah. I know why you want a new suit. I said, How did you know I wanted a new suit? He said, Because Louis Armstrong is in town. That's in the levee days, ... and a cat by the name of Red. So we had a date and he had to make a lot of change of cars to get to Webster Groves so Red was always my boy, around Grand Central.
You don't know his other name, just Red?
Red, that was good enough. ... If I didn't have

enough enough money, I'd pay him the next time. I was his boy. I always had some money. So one night I run into Red and he said, No, man, I ain't going to take you nowhere. I said, What you mean by that? ... take me five nights a week, you damn near going to take on salary. I mean what you mean. He said, Man, I ain't/you nowhere. I said, You not going to take me nowhere. No. I said, Armstrong's Why? He said, Louis Armenstreng in town. And this is his private cab. And I said, I'll be damn. I told Pops that and he screamed. Now, musically what happened ...
